proofs: Prepared-only reversal requires its own authorization, exact source, original adoption request and stable reversal UUID.
Remote proof is READ ONLY; any allocator namespace/guard, existing assignments, active allocator or schema/integrity failure refuses reversal.
Original admissions and adoption metadata remain; mapped payloads, original hashes and admission request IDs are unchanged.
Frozen historical outbox, records, receipts, confirmed count, quarantine and existing corporate rows are preserved.
Each legacy materialization commits records/outbox, admission flag, ID mapping and batch evidence atomically.
Batch rollback, interruption after committed progress, process restart and uncertain intent/batch/completion commits recover without duplicate IDs or payload replacement.
A prior exact mapping is recognized without a new nextval or historical update.
Capture persistence, delivery and resume are fenced during each batch; captures may proceed between batches and their new admissions are included.
A session fence rejects concurrent reversion processes; changed approvals or request IDs cannot overwrite the recovery.
Delivery stays paused and blocked through materialization; resume also requires validation persisted by the existing collision-recovery operation.
New legacy collisions remain pending and can be selectively quarantined before valid rows are delivered.
Compiled CLI was executed and repeated successfully in the disposable fixture.
Local migration 008 trigger remains installed; no DROP TRIGGER, manual control update, setval or ALTER SEQUENCE is part of recovery.
limits: Returning to a local sequence does not guarantee global exclusivity with MADM; recurring collisions still require existing selective quarantine and validation.
No production counts, privileges, latency or materialization throughput were verified; test datasets are smaller than the reported 12270 admissions.
Sequence numbers consumed by a rolled-back transaction can leave normal gaps; committed IDs are never remapped.
The same updated worker must run this code; a new CLI beside the old binary is insufficient.
This is not a rollback of an active or remotely installed allocator; uncertain remote authority is preserved and blocks the procedure.
